commentary.seminaVerbi:
The queen arrives as an intelligent outsider who refuses secondhand awe. She tests, watches, then loses her breath—not from mysticism but from coherence: speech, architecture, ritual, labor, and justice all fit together. Admiration here is psychological surrender to integration; she meets a mind whose inner order has successfully turned into public order.

Mark’s diagnosis turns the same lens inward. The real impurity is not contagion but emission; what stains you is what your heart manufactures. The scene is an argument against scapegoating the world for one’s own interior disarray. External splendor can impress, but the true court is inside, and its ministers are thoughts.

Speculation: this convergence echoes Stoic ethics where virtue is the only real good and vice is an inner failure, not a thing caught. It also resembles Buddhist emphasis on mind as the source of suffering and harm, and the Upanishadic turn from outer ritual to inner reality. In Sufism, the polished heart as mirror fits the same intuition: what you see and do flows from what you are.
commentary.excursus:
The Queen of Saba comes with “hard questions,” but the text keeps slipping from inquiry into appetite. She arrives as a convoy of scent and weight, and when she finally “spoke to him all that she had in her heart,” Solomon answers everything, not like a sage but like a perfect mirror. What undoes her is not truth but total coherence: the house, the table, the uniforms, the choreography, even the holocausts. Order so complete it steals her breath. She has “no longer any spirit in her” because the system leaves no crack for her own interior to stay hers.

She blesses his God and pays him, but it reads like tribute to the spell, not conversion. The spices are the giveaway: desire packaged as piety, intimacy converted into commodity. Solomon’s wisdom is a machine that can digest whatever a foreign heart confesses and return it as admiration.

Jesus cuts against that spectacle. He drags defilement away from foods and rituals and locates it where Solomon’s empire dares not look: the heart that manufactures its own sewage. Nothing “without” can stain you, he says, because the real contamination is the private production line of thoughts, lusts, greed, and the “evil eye”—envy’s hungry stare. The queen is dazzled by a holiness you can see and smell; Jesus insists the dread is invisible, the rot is domestic, and the enemy is not the strange thing you take in but the familiar thing that comes out of you.
commentary.synthesis: God’s gifts can be publicly legible as ordered wisdom, but impurity is not imported; it is generated by the heart and therefore judged at the source.

gospel.text: Jesus splits audience and disciples to expose a literacy gap: public aphorism, then private interrogation, then rebuke. The teaching relocates moral gravity from boundary-maintenance to interior governance, collapsing the authority of tradition when it mistakes ritual perimeter for moral center.

reading.text: The scene is international verification of Israel’s order: architecture, administration, and speech cohere into a single public witness. The foreign queen’s confession functions as external accreditation—Israel’s God is confessed by an outsider precisely through Israel’s visible coherence.

marginalia.text: Fame “in the name of the LORD”: renown is treated as a theological fact, not PR.
She brings caravan-wealth and also “all that she had in her heart”: tribute and testimony yoked.
Omniscience by proxy: the king is “ignorant of” nothing asked—wisdom as total coverage.
The inventory culminates in worship (“holocausts”): liturgy is part of the argument. Awe becomes collapse: “no longer any spirit.”
Empiricism converts hearsay: the half-report motif shames distance and secondhand religion.
Her blessing maps politics to ethics: throne justified only by “judgment and justice.”
Gifts answer splendor with surplus; the spice note is excess quantified—astonishment turned into offering.
Defilement reversed: outside does not stain; the self is the source of its own uncleanness.
Blunt physiology (“privy”) demystifies taboo: purity rules are reduced to digestion.
The heart is a factory: interiority produces acts before acts appear.
Catalogue theology: sin named in plural, social and private; “evil eye” makes envy visible.
Verdict repeated: “from within” is both origin and accusation—no scapegoat in food or contact.

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Keep watch, Lord, with unceasing love over your family; protect and defend it always, since it has placed its hope in you alone. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, and is God for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Matins

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Lord God, our Savior, grant us your help, that we may always desire the works of light and do what is true; so that we who have been born of you as children of light may be your witnesses before all people. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Lauds

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Lord, holy Father, faithful God, who sent the promised Holy Spirit to gather together the people whom sin had scattered, help us to be, in the midst of the world, a leaven of unity and peace. Through Jesus Christ our Lord.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Terce

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Almighty and loving God, who at the midpoint of our day grant rest from our weariness, look with favor upon the work we have begun today, remedy our shortcomings, and make our deeds pleasing to you. Through Jesus Christ our Lord.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Sext

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, who for the salvation of mankind stretched out your arms upon the cross, grant that all our actions may be pleasing to you and serve to make your redemption known to the world. You who live and reign for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Nones

hoursOfPrayer.prayer: Hear, O Lord, our supplications and protect us by day and by night; you who are unchanging, grant steadfastness always to us who live subject to the succession of times and hours. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Vespers

hoursOfPrayer.prayer:
Let us pray:
Lord Jesus Christ, you are meek and humble of heart and you offer those who come to you a gentle yoke and a light burden; deign, then, to accept the desires and the deeds of the day we have ended. Grant that we may rest through the night, so that, our body and spirit renewed, we may persevere steadfastly in your service. You who live and reign for ever and ever.
hoursOfPrayer.label: Compline

lines: And the queen of Saba having heard of the fame of Solomon in the name of the Lord, came to try him with hard questions.

And entering into Jerusalem with a great train, and riches, and camels that carried spices, and an immense quantity of gold, and precious stones, she came to king Solomon, and spoke to him all that she had in her heart.
And Solomon informed her of all the things she proposed to him: there was not any word the king was ignorant of, and which he could not answer her.
And when the queen of Saba saw all the wisdom of Solomon, and the house which he had built,

And the meat of his table, and the apartments of his servants, and the order of his ministers, and their apparel, and the cupbearers, and the holocausts, which he offered in the house of the Lord, she had no longer any spirit in her;
And she said to the king: The report is true, which I heard in my own country,

Concerning thy words, and concerning thy wisdom. And I did not believe them that told me, till I came myself, and saw with my own eyes, and have found that the half hath not been told me: thy wisdom and thy works exceed the fame which I heard.
Blessed are thy men, and blessed are thy servants, who stand before thee always, and hear thy wisdom.

Blessed be the Lord thy God, whom thou hast pleased, and who hath set thee upon the throne of Israel, because the Lord hath loved Israel for ever, and hath appointed thee king, to do judgment and justice.

And she gave the king a hundred and twenty talents of gold, and of spices a very great store, and precious stones: there was brought no more such abundance of spices as these which the queen of Saba gave to king Solomon.

lines: And calling again the multitude unto him, he said to them: Hear ye me all and understand.
There is nothing from without a man that entering into him can defile him. But the things which come from a man, those are they that defile a man.
If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
And when he was come into the house from the multitude, his disciples asked him the parable.
And he saith to them: So are you also without knowledge? Understand you not that every thing from without entering into a man cannot defile him:
Because it entereth not into his heart but goeth into his belly and goeth out into the privy, purging all meats?
But he said that the things which come out from a man, they defile a man.
For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness.
All these evil things come from within and defile a man.
readings.heading: From the Gospel according to Mark
